scenes.line1: Ever deleted a commit by accident?
scenes.line2: How do you get it back?
scenes.say: Ever deleted a commit by accident? How do you get it back in Git?
Reset moves your branch pointer and can erase commits. Revert makes a new commit that undoes changes, which is safer when others share your branch.

scenes.label: Restore
scenes.sub: Recovers files or branches you lost.
scenes.say: Restore brings back files or even entire branches that you accidentally removed.

scenes.title: Using Reflog
scenes.say: Reflog shows every move your branch made, so you can find and recover lost commits even after a reset.

scenes.question: Is reset safe for shared branches?
scenes.right: No, use revert for shared history to avoid trouble.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: Is reset safe for shared branches? No way. Use revert instead to keep everyone in sync.
